Good afternoon. This cheese looks interesting. What is it?
It is Queijo Canastra. It comes from the mountains of Minas Gerais, and it is part of our heritage.
It has a wonderful flavor. How long do you age it?
Usually for a few weeks. Unlike Parmigiano, it is ready quickly. What makes it unique is the terroir.

Good morning, and welcome to our dairy. My family makes Parmigiano-Reggiano here, near Parma, and we use the same method as my grandfather. The cheese has only three ingredients: milk, salt, and rennet. Every morning, we use the fresh milk from cows in this region. Then, we put each cheese in salt water for about three weeks. After that, we age the cheese for at least twelve months. Some of our cheeses age for two or three years. At the end, an expert checks every cheese. If the cheese is perfect, it gets a special mark. This mark shows that the cheese is authentic. Now, please follow me, and you can taste it.

Welcome back to Travel and Taste. Today, we talk about food and memory. When Brazilians live abroad, what do they miss? Many of them say: Brazilian coffee and cheese bread. For them, these foods are a taste of home. They bring back memories of the family and of the place where they grew up. This is why regional products are so powerful. They are not only food. They are culture. And this is why food fairs are important. At a fair, visitors can taste the product and hear its story. A good story makes people remember the product, and the place it comes from.

First, I say the name of the product and where it comes from. Then, I explain how it is traditionally made. Next, I say what makes it unique, like its terroir. After that, I compare it with an Italian product that my partner knows. Finally, I connect the product to the heritage of its region.
